passages.context: The article's account of napkins at Greek and Roman meals, read in the retrieved transcription in full. Registered as a material negative as well as a positive: the article covers the materials, sizes, uses and even the wearing of napkins as head-dress, and records no signalling function of any kind at table.
passages.notes: The article's Greek equivalents and its parenthetical classical citations, including Xen. Cyrop. I.3 51, Quintil. I.5 57, Hor. Sat. II.4.81 and II.8.63, and Martial XII.29 and XIV.138, are omitted from the transcription and were not checked at those loci.

work.author: William Smith, editor
work.description: The standard nineteenth-century English dictionary of classical realia. Its article Mantele describes the napkins used at Greek and Roman meals, including the mappa that guests brought with them to the table, and records no signalling function for any of them. Registered as an identified working authority on Greco-Roman dining, not as modern scholarship. Loci are article headwords.
work.title: A Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities
